story.head: The Blackhawks are on a heater
paras: The Blackhawks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-2 in Chicago on Oct 6. The Blues (14-9-3) beat Dallas 5-3 on Nov 27, and the Blackhawks have won four straight. The Hawks played last night, and the Blues are rested. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Blackhawks last (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Blues sixth (tied for 14th). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Blackhawks get their shots through better than almost anyone (2nd), but don’t block many shots (31st) and have struggled on the power play (31st). Chicago has allowed 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Blues keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd). They also get the league’s best looks (1st), so the Blues wait for good looks, but the Blackhawks settle for hopeful ones.

Roman Kantserov (15 G / 5 A / 20 P in 26 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Sam Rinzel (2 G / 16 A / 18 P in 25 GP) is next in line. For the Blues, Robert Thomas (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 26 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games. Dylan Holloway (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 26 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with seven points in his last five games.
Drew Commesso (1-0-0 / .880 SV% in 1 GS) is in line to start for Chicago. Joel Hofer (11-6-2 / .919 SV% in 19 GS) has been terrific for St. Louis and will likely start.

At home, Jim Montgomery likes to send Toropchenko, Suter and Dvorský out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Mangiapane, Greene and Boucher. Elsewhere, the Blues usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
